Commentary.Commentary: Fifties from Devon Smith and Shane Dowrich gave some sort of stability to the home side. A useful knock from Roston Chase also gave them some momentum. However, the inability to convert the starts into big ones meant that the home side couldn't run away with the game. With around 35 minutes to go, it will be a stern test for the visiting batsmen. Will the hosts make early inroads? Or will the tourists show grit and determination? Join us shortly for Sri Lanka's second essay with the bat.

So, 47 is the lead that the hosts have managed to accumulate. Doesn't seem to be a threatening one but it can still prove to be valuable on a surface which still has something on it for the pace bowlers. The visitors came back nicely after the Tea break and took the last five wickets for only 46 runs. Kumara was the pick of the bowlers as he took a 4-fer and he got good support from Rajitha and Lakmal who took 3 and 2 wickets respectively to help their side's cause.

OUT! Brilliant catch to end the innings! Shortish ball on off, Gabriel goes for the big pull across the line but gets a top edge that goes over the slip cordon. The keeper and a couple of fielders are running after it. However, de Silva calls for it, keeps his eyes on the balls, takes it really well and then tumbles down. WEST INDIES ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 300!

The last pair is having a bit of fun. Gabriel backs away and heaves it off the inner half of the bat through square leg. A couple of runs is the result. 300 is up for the hosts and it is met with appreciation from the crowd.
Shortish ball on middle, Gabriel goes for a full-fledged pull but has no timing behind it whatsoever. Ends up mistiming it past the short leg fielder.
Pitched up ball around off, hit away towards long on for a single. The lead moves onto 45.
Much better from the No. 11! Back of a length ball on middle and leg, Gabriel is right behind it in defense.
So close! On a good length outside off, angling in. Gabriel is late to react as he swings aimlessly at it but misses. That went past the off pole by a whisker.
Shortish delivery, heaved away to the mid-wicket region for a single.
FOUR! This one has been hit with authority. The first time he has made good contact with the bat. In the zone for Cummins. He makes some room and hits it hard over mid on to find the fence.
Fullish delivery around off, Miguel tries to defend it but gets foxed.
Back of a length ball, Shannon goes for an ambitious shot but mistimes it back towards the bowler.
Welcomes Gabriel with a short ball. He ducks under it.
Shannon Gabriel is the last man in.

OUT! Kumara gets his third! He has been fiery and has got the results. He sees Roach shuffling across his stumps and hence, opts to bowl full and fast. The batsman fails to flick it away and is hit on the pads. An appeal follows and up goes the umpire's finger. Roach doesn't go for the review, it looked dead to the naked eye.
Backs away to the fullish delivery and mistimes his heave towards mid-wicket. A run taken.
Kumara is steaming in and bending his back. Another uncomfortable moment for Cummins who ducks under it somehow.

Close shave! Short of a length ball attacking the rib-cage area of the batsman. He tucks it awkwardly towards short leg. The fielder has a shy at the stumps but misses. Replays show that even if that hit, he might have been safe.
Another swing and a miss! Back of a length outside off, Roach tries to slog it away but fails.

A loud appeal for an LBW denied! Good length ball, seaming in. Roach tries to block it but misses to get pinged on the back pad. Lakmal appeals but the umpire stays put. Seems that it was going down leg.

FOUR! Hammered! Now, that is a batsman's shot! On a length and width on offer, Roach clears his front leg and slaps it through cover-point. The fielder in the deep moves to his right but has no chance of stopping it. These are valuable runs for the Windies, the lead moves to 38.
Solid as a rock this time! Short of a length ball on middle and leg, Kemar makes use of the depth of the crease and answers it with a straight bat.
Roach missed out there! Gets a juicy full toss outside off, he goes perhaps too hard at it as he has been doing throughout and gets beaten.
Fuller length ball around off, Roach covers the line and defends it solidly.
Suranga Lakmal is back into the attack for a burst.

Full delivery attacking the base of the stumps, Miguel backs away and goes for a hit down the ground but mistimes it back to the bowler. Kumara picks it up and has a wild shy at the stumps. Has some piece of advice for the tailender. Aleem Dar tells him to calm down.
The physio attends to Cummins. He needs to be careful. He is an important bowler for the hosts. Looks to be alright at the moment.

Ouch, that will sting! He misjudged the length completely. Good length ball on middle and off, Cummins tries to duck under it but is hit flush on the grille of the helmet. Takes some time to gather himself as Ian Gould comes across to check on him.
Kumara attacks the stumps with a full length ball. Cummins defends it down the track.
Good length delivery from around the wicket. It is around the off stump as Cummins backs away and goes for an agricultural slog across the line but misses it by a mile.
On a length outside off, Kemar taps it past cover-point for a single.
In the arc for Roach. He shuffles and goes for an ambitious stroke through the line but only manages to connect with thin air.
Time for Drinks.
Comes down the track to send it out of the universe but luckily, he couldn't make connection.
There is a fly slip in place.
Short and targeting the grille, misses the edge somehow.
Roach works it to the leg side and changes strike.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Jagging back into the batsman who calmly blocks it back to the bowler.
Short and wide, Roach goes after it but misses.
Umpire Ian Gould is having another look at the ball. Seems to be fine.
And another short ball to end the over. The batsman is happy to get under it and leave it for the keeper.
Unusual bounce. Too high to worry the batsman! The umpire has signalled a wide.
Fourth consecutive short of a length delivery from Kumara. Cummins is the target again but he does well to evade it and duck under it in time.
Moves away and flashes hard but fails to put bat to ball.

Playing fire with fire! Lahiru dishes in another short ball angled into the body of the batsman. Cummins hangs back in his crease and connects the pull shot nicely. Chandimal at short mid-wicket is in a good position to stop but a misfield means two runs are taken.
Another taste of sweet chin music. Nicely left alone by Cummins this time.
Back of a length on the pads and flicked through square leg. Batsmen take three before the ball is cut out inside the boundary line.
Lahiru Kumara is back into the attack.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Bumper to start with. A rather unwelcoming welcome for Cummins. Rajitha goes around the wicket to the new batsman, digs it in and angles it into his body. Cummins ducks under it in desperation, and the ball flicks his arm before reaching the keeper. The Sri Lankan team appeals in unison but Ian Gould ignores it. Can't take the review as they have none left.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Miguel Cummins is the new batsman.

OUT! BOOM! Another one bites the dust. This time, it is the Windies skipper. Rajitha has been persistent with the back of a length delivery outside off. Dishes another one for the batsman and he goes after it. The hanging bat of Holder manages to kiss the ball through to Dickwella behind the stumps.
Stays on his front foot and blocks it to the off side.
The ball is way wide on the leg side but the batsman still goes after it and misses.
Third man in place now.
Roach shoulders arms to let that one through, finally!
It is almost comical what Roach is trying to do here. He takes quick steps across his stumps and pushes the full delivery to mid on.
FOUR! Some width on offer and Roach throws his hands at it. The ball flies off the edge and to the third man boundary. Roach can frustrate the opposition with some quick runs here.
The batsman tries flicking a ball that is down the leg side.
Shuffles across his stumps and somehow gets it to square leg. One run added to the total.
Starts with a fuller delivery on the pads, the batsman flicks to square leg for a couple.
Goes after a wide delivery, a wild hoick but misses.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Punched off the back foot to the off side and a single taken.

FOUR! Flashes and flashes hard! No half measure from the Windies skipper. Gets a wide full delivery and he goes for the drive with hard hands. The ball flies off the outside edge and races to the boundary past the gully fielder.
Back of a length around off and punched off the back foot for nothing.
Touch fuller and outside off, Holder goes for the cover drive but mistimes it.
Outside off on a good length, left alone.

Bye! Almost five more runs but not to be. Holder lets the good length delivery outside off to the keeper who dives to his left to collect it. But the low bounce means that it doesn't carry and goes through his gloves and almost hits the helmet behind him. In the end, just one run.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Drags his length back and the batsman blocks it off the back foot.
A touch fuller around off and pushed to covers for nothing.
And comes back with a peach! An absolute jaffa. Keeps it on a back of a length around off and makes Holder hop. He tries to fend at it but misses the ball. Lucky escape!

Five wides! Too short and way over the batsman's head. Keeper tries to cut it but even he is unable to reach it. The ball goes to the boundary and the umpire signals a wide. Free runs for Windies and the lead is into the double digits now.
Holder pulls out at the last moment while the bowler was about to deliver the ball. A sightscreen issue was the reason behind it.
Kemar Roach strides out to bat.

OUT! And the gruesome innings of Devendra Bishoo comes to an end. Rajitha lands it on a fuller length outside off and the batsman goes for the drive which isn't there. Gets a thick outside edge and Kusal Mendis at second slip pouches the ball quite easily.
Hangs back in his crease and pushed it to point fielder.
Pushed through from an inward angle and wraps Bishoo on the chest guard, who wanted to play the pull.
Outside off and blocked to the off side.
Back of a length around leg, Holder gets it to leg side and takes a single.
Starts with a wayward delivery on pads and the batsman clips it to leg side for nothing.
Too good for Bishoo to make any contact. On a good length outside off and coming in with the angle. Bishoo plays the line but misses and the ball whizzes past his outside edge.
Touch too straight and on the hips, Holder clips it to leg side and changes strike.

Two deliveries prior to this one came in and this one held its line. Beautiful set up from the fast bowler. Hooks Holder with a full driveable length delivery around off, who goes for it but fails to make connection.
Keeping the line of attack as straight as possible. Full around middle and leg, the batsman pushes it down the ground and Lakmal gets down to stop it.
Full and outside off. Punched through covers from Holder and two runs are taken.

Lakmal starts from 'round the wicket as well, targeting the stumps of the left-hander. Dishes it on a full length, angling into the batsman, who pushes it to mid on. Misfield means a single is taken eventually.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Outside off on a similar length, Bishoo pushes it through covers and opens his account.
Changes the angle and goes around the wicket to bring the ball in to the left-hander from a good length. The batsman blocks it to the off side.
Short of a length outside off, punched to mid on for nothing.
Short and into the body, Bishoo ducks under it.
On a good length around off and pushed to covers for a single.
Back of a length around off and nicely defended by the batsman.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Chin music for Bishoo to start with who does well to sway away and leave it.
Devendra Bishoo is the new man in. This is his 50th Test innings. The Windies need a vital contribution from him. Meanwhile, a man comes under the lid at short leg.

OUT! Gone! Big fish has been hooked in! Lakmal kept probing outside off on a good length and finally got his reward. Dowrich has to play at the delivery as it is coming in with the angle but it moves away at the last moment. A feather edge results and a simple catch to the keeper. Windies lose their sixth and Sri Lanka are into the tail now. A gutsy knock from the wicket-keeper batsman nonetheless.
Similar line and length, pushed to covers off the back foot.
On a good length outside off, Holder pokes at the ball and manages to get it in the vacant point region. One run added to the total.
Presents the full face and defends the full delivery back to the bowler.
The batsman defends it from within the crease to the off side.

FOUR! Almost, almost had him. Squares him up with a peach from wide of the crease. It is on a good length and comes into the body with the angle and moves away after pitching. Dowrich hangs his bat in anticipation and the ball flies off the outside edge past the left side of the fielder at gully. No one is in the deep at third man which means a boundary for the Windies. Scores are level now.
Another delivery outside off, left alone by the batsman.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

6th Test fifty for Shane Dowrich! Short and into the body of the wicket-keeper batsman who goes for the pull but doesn't get it off the middle. The ball goes past the fielder at mid on, down the ground and two runs are taken before the fielder cuts it off. It has been a very good knock from Dowrich. Gets a round of applause from the Windies camp.
Hangs back in his crease and blocks the full ball with a straight bat.
On a driveable length outside off and pushed through covers by Dowrich. One run added to the total.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Change of bat for Dowrich.
Drives the full ball down the ground and changes strike.
OOH! Close. Serves it on a fuller length once again and keeps it in the channel of uncertainty outside off. Holder hangs his bat and misses the line. Good thing for him that he didn't edge it.
On a fullish length, just outside off. Holder pushes it to covers for nothing.
Suranga Lakmal is into the attack now.
Full around off, mistimes the drive to the off side.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

FOUR! Crisp! That is the word for this shot. Full around off, moving in the air and off the pitch as well. Dowrich covers the line and pushes it past the bowler. The connection is good and the ball races to the long off boundary. Trail now into single digit.
Similar length but errs in line. The ball goes down the leg side to the keeper.
Full around off, pushed to covers for nothing.
Some shape on this one. Touch short and outside off and it seams after pitching. Dowrich gets his bat behind the line and pushes it to point.
Makes the batsman play the fuller ball down the pitch. Good start to the evening session from Kumara.
Too short and wide, Holder ignores it.
Similar length around off, blocked off the front foot.
Full and down the leg side again. Holder couldn't flick it as the ball thuds into keeper's gloves.
Corrects his line and serves it on a fuller length outside off. The batsman keeps his bat away and lets it through.
Back of a length, down the leg side, Holder fails to get bat on it.
We are back for the evening session. Shane Dowrich and Jason Holder to resume their innings. Lahiru Kumara will continue his spell.
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

Session highlights - 25 overs, 87 runs, 2 wickets. The hosts continue to control the game. They have scored runs at a good clip and have brought the trail down to only 12 runs. Still, there is quite some batting to come and they will be aiming to take the game further away from the visitors. Shane Dowrich has played a gutsy knock so far and the home side will want him to carry on. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, need to be more disciplined. Lahiru Kumara has struck once with the second new ball but the tourists still need to take wickets in a heap if they are to stay in the contest. Join us shortly for the final session.
Full length ball outside off, shaping away. Dowrich doesn't fiddle with it. THAT IS TEA ON DAY 3!
On a short of a length and seaming away after pitching. Dowrich keeps his bat close to his body and lets it be.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
He gets one to point finally. Back of a length again outside off and slapped from the back foot for nothing.
Similar length and closer to the off stump, the batsman goes for the cut once again but misses. The ball goes past the outside edge. Do they really need to take such risk before Tea?
Touch short and outside off, Dowrich goes with hard hands but it hits the bottom edge of his bat and falls on the ground.
Kasun Rajitha to share the new ball from the other end.
Outside off and left alone for the keeper.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
The skipper, Jason Holder is the new man in.

OUT! Now, now, now! The brand new cherry has done the trick. The 78-run partnership is broken. Windies lose a wicket at the stroke of Lunch. Lapse in concentration perhaps? Whatever is was, it has worked in the visitors' favor. Coming to the delivery, Lahiru puts it on a fullish length on middle and leg. The ball seams after pitching and Chase goes through with a full-blooded flick. He gets it from the middle of the bat but can't get it over Lakmal standing at short mid-wicket who takes it safely. The hosts are behind by only 12 runs.
Well outside off and left alone.
Similar length just outside off, driven on the up through covers for a brace.
Kumara gets the new ball and bowls a full on around off. Chase drives it tentatively down the ground.
The second new ball is due and it has been taken straightaway. Sri Lanka need to pick up quick wickets.
Hangs back and blocks it to end the over.
Flighted around middle and leg, Dowrich sweeps but finds the short square leg fielder.
The batsman dances down the track and does well to block the ball.
Touch short from Akila outside off. The batsman cuts it off the back foot behind point. One run taken.
Chase has played it towards mid-wicket.
Starts with a wrong' un on stumps and driven to long on for a quick single.
Too straight from Lahiru and tucked away behind square for two.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
On a fuller length on off and the batsman drives it to mid off.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! This is what you call awareness. Toying with the fast bowler here. Kumara goes to short of a length, keeps it outside off and angles it in. The extra effort from the bowler means that the ball rises but Chase rides the bounce and guides it nicely through the gap between gully and slip cordon. Runs are coming thick and fast for both the batsmen now.
Chase is middling 'em more often than not. He creams another drive but straight to the fielder at covers.
Floated on leg and flicked to backward square for a single.
Driven towards the mid on region. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Damn! How easily he drove it? Windies are upping the ante it seems. Akila gives a lot of air outside off and Dowrich drives it between the cover and mid off fielder for a boundary.
Pushed through outside off and the batsman chops it behind point for two.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Works the flighted delivery to the leg side and completes a single.
Four Byes! Dishes one on a back of a length and angles it into the batsman but it goes down the leg side. It brushes his thigh pad and goes fine to the boundary.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Back of a length ball, kept out watchfully.
Touch too straight. Strays down the leg side and flicked off the pads. Two more runs added to the total.
Kumara bowls an effort delivery outside off. Keeps it on a back of a length and Dowrich flashes hard. The ball takes extra bounce and goes over the bat to the keeper.
Down the leg side, no trouble at all for the batsman.
Lahiru Kumara is back on.
Nice looking lofted straight drive to the fuller delivery. The fielder at long on cuts it to one run.
Another sweep to the loopy delivery and it goes to the square leg region. A brace added to the total.
Drives the flighted delivery through the cover region and takes a single. This also brings up the fifty partnership between the two. Good going from the duo.
Tossed up on leg and played to mid-wicket for nothing.
The short of length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side. They pick up a single.
Short and down the leg side. Dowrich sweep it fine for a single.
Skidding through after pitching, Chase goes back and defends it solidly.
Slips in the wrong one. Chase reads it off the pitch and guides it towards point.
Fuller in length this time, knocked down with ease to long on for a single.
On a flatter trajectory again, dealt with from deep within the crease.
Shorter in length, kept out off the back foot.
Tossed up on middle and leg, defended solidly off the front foot.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.

WOW! A peach out of nowhere. Tosses it up outside off and the drift takes it further away. The batsman is committed to the forward defense but can't reach the delivery. In the end, he misses it and the keeper whips the bails in a flash. Good thing he didn't come out of his crease.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flighted, outside off and driven to cover fielder.
Nudges it to the leg side and completes another single.
Short and wide and cut away through point. One run added to the total.

Almost, almost gets in trouble. Intelligent stuff from Akila. He pushes this one quicker and Dowrich moves his right leg and flicks it from the back foot. Had he missed the ball, it would have been plumb. In the end, one run taken.
Dowrich plays it to the point region.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Entices Dowrich with a flighted wider delivery. He gets right behind the line and defends it.
Flighted on stumps and the batsman blocks it off the front foot.
Touch short and outside off, played to point region for nothing.
Change of ends for Akila Dananjaya.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter and touch short, Chase defends it off the front foot.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Touch short and pulls it to deep mid-wicket. One run added.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
Flatter on middle and leg, punched to mid-wicket for nothing.
Dhananjaya de Silva comes into the attack.
Short of a length, punched to cover-point.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Back of a length outside off, played to gully from the bottom edge.
Mistimes the pull. It is short of a length outside off and Dowrich looks to go across but doesn't get the connection.
Drags his length back, outside off and Chase dabs it through point region and takes a single.
Tentative push from the crease but misses the delivery on a driveable length. The ball misses the outside edge and thuds into the kepeer's gloves.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Touch short and easily clipped to the leg side for a couple. The fielder throws it too close to the keeper, who is unable to gather it. An overthrow results as well. 200 up for the Windies.
Another google on middle and flicked off his pads to the leg side. One run taken.

FOUR! He is reading the finger spinner quite easily now. He bowls a wrong one around off and it goes the other way. The batsman rocks back in his crease and cuts it through cover-point. No one has any chance of stopping that crisp stroke.

SIX! Going, going and gone! Dowrich dealing in boundaries. Akila gives it some air but errs in line. The batsman takes a couple of steps down the pitch and lofts it over mid on. Good intent from the batsman and some quick runs for the Windies.
Pushed through on middle and blocked off the back foot to the off side.
Outside off, third leave in a row.
The uneven nature of the track is once again on display. On a length outside off, stays low. Roston doesn't fiddle with it.
This one is well outside off, left alone.
Fuller in length on middle and leg, played defensively towards square leg.
FOUR! Well played! Short and room on offer, Chase stands tall and slaps it through the point region. The timing is spot on and he gets the desired result.
On a length outside off, defended from within the crease.

Statement from SLC on 'Changing the condition of the Ball' - The team management has informed us that Sri Lankan players have not engaged in any wrongdoing during the ongoing Test match. SLC advised the team to take the field to ensure the continuity of the match and wish to commend the decision taken by the team to continue with the game 'under protest' to ensure the upholding of the spirit of the game.
Time for Drinks. Meanwhile, Kasun Rajitha is back for a bowl.
This one goes the other way. But the batsman reads it nicely and defends it off the front foot.
Conventional leg break around leg, Dowrich tries to flick it but gets hit on his pads.
Akila bowls a floater and nicely defended by Dowrich off the front foot.
Flatter around off and middle and pushed to the leg side for nothing.
Touch short and punched to mid-wicket off the pads.
This one is down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.
Back of a length once again and seaming in sharply to hit his thigh pad. Chase is in a bit of tangle but no harm done.
Short and well outside off, the batsman shoulders his arms.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Lands it around off on a good length. Chase slaps it to point for nothing.
Hangs back in his crease and keeps it down off the back foot.
Back of a length outside off and crunched through cover-point for a couple.

FOUR! Up and over. Dowrich changing gears and getting into the spinner. Gets a tossed up delivery around middle, comes down the ground and lifts it over mid on for a boundary. Doesn't look to hit it too hard.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Touch short and on the leg side, the batsman sweeps it. The fielder at short square leg dives to his right to stop the ball and does well to get his hand to it. A brace results.
Tossed up around off and middle, driven to mid on for nothing.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up on middle and blocked down the pitch.
Full around off and nicely driven off the front foot through covers. The ball rolls through the infield and stops inside the boundary. In the end, three runs are taken.
Outside off and Dowrich keeps his bat close to his body to let is pass.

Lakmal lands it outside off, on a good length and the ball seams in sharply. The batsman is beaten all ends up and gets hit on his thigh pad. Some excited appeal from the fielding team but umpire is unmoved.
Nothing doing with the wider delivery. Left alone for the keeper.
Back of a length and defended off the back foot to short mid-wicket.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Looks to punch the shorter delivery off the back foot but doesn't get it cleanly.
Another flighted delivery on middle and pushed off the pads for nothing.

FOUR! Loopy delivery on middle and leg, Chase gives charge and lifts it over the infield from the inside half of the bat. The fielder at mid-wicket runs to his left but the ball has enough legs to go to the boundary.
Plants his foot down and turns it to short mid-wicket for nothing.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Flighted outside off, on a driveable length and Dowrich obliges. The ball drifts away just a touch after landing and takes the thick outside edge of blade. The fielder at slip dives to his right but couldn't stop the ball as it goes to third man. Three runs added to the total.
Short of a length, angling into the body, the batsman tucks it to square leg. One run added to the total.
Back of a length and well outside off to entice Dowrich with a shot.
Back of a length coming into the batsman, who does well to push it to mid-wicket.
Skids through the back of a length area into the batsman. An inside edge is induced but misses the stumps. No harm done in the end.
Touch too straight on a similar length. Chase flicks it to fine leg to change the strike.
Lands it on a good length outside off and Chase lets it pass.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Pushed through, on middle and flicked to short mid-wicket for nothing.
Floater on middle, pushed to mid on for nothing.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Flighted outside and driven to the fielder at mid off who make a good diving stop.
Short of a length outside off and Chase cuts it to point for nothing.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Touch fuller and jagging back from outside off into the stump after pitching. Chase does well to get behind the line to defend it.
On a good length around off, Chase presents the full face to block it to  the off side.
Back of a length ball, angling in sharply. Chase hangs back and tucks it with a closed bat face towards mid-wicket.
On a length outside off, played with an angled bat towards the point region.
Suranga Lakmal to continue.
The batsman works it down the leg side for nothing.
Flatter outside off and Chase cuts it fine to backward point region for another single.
On the shorter side outside off and cut away to the deep backward point fielder for a single.
Similar length and nicely defended by Dowrich.
Floater around off, defended back to the bowler.
We are about to get on with the session after a brief delay. Players are coming out to the middle. Shane Dowrich joins Roston Chase in the middle. Akila Dananjaya to continue with his over.
Update 1325 Local - Oh no! It has started drizzling and the groundsmen rush in with the blue covers. Let us hope it is a passing shower.

OUT! Plumb in front! Dananjaya gets his first wicket. This is what Sri Lanka need to do, keep on chipping away at the wickets. The offie tosses this one nicely from around the stumps. It is outside off as Smith leans ahead to defend. However, his foot movement is not that assured and he ends up playing down the wrong line, the in-drift causing the same. As a result, he is struck on the pads and the visitors go up in unison. The umpire obliges as well. Smith doesn't take a review. Even if he did, it wouldn't have mattered as the Hawk Eye shows three reds. He departs after playing a good knock.
Swinging down the leg side, tucked towards backward square leg for a single.
Lakmal once again lands it in the avenue of apprehension and gets the ball to seam back in. Smith watches it closely and makes a good leave.
The southpaw hangs back to the short of the length ball and blocks it nicely towards cover-point.
Another play and a miss! A touch fuller this time outside off, shaping in. Smith comes forward tentatively and goes for a tame push through the line but gets foxed. He needs to be careful.
In the zone outside off, holding its line. Devon points his bat skywards to let it be.

Brilliant ball! Lakmal runs in from around the wicket and bowls a good length ball in the corridor of uncertainty. The ball moves away after pitching, the wind also aids the cause. Smith tries to defend it but is beaten all ends up.
Suranga Lakmal to bowl from the other end.
FOUR! As smooth as you like from Roston Chase. Gets another flighted delivery outside off and creams the cover drive. A welcome boundary for the right-hander.
Well, it has turned overcast all of a sudden. The groundsmen are getting ready with the covers.
Another loopy delivery around middle and leg, Chase pushes it to square leg for nothing.
Floater around off, defended off the back foot.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.
FOUR! Aggressive start from Chase. Goes after the tossed up delivery and plays it to the square leg boundary. Welcome back, Akila.
Flighted one around off and blocked off the back foot.
Both set of players are making their way to the middle. Roston Chase will take the strike while Akila Dananjaya will take the ball after the break.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

And that brings the end to one of the most wrangling sessions. After 120 minutes of drama, flying tempers and reluctance, we finally had the start of play. Sri Lanka were the guilty party and they paid the price as well, and not just in terms of the penalty but in kind as well. Their reputation has been put on the line, which their bowlers can save from shredding to pieces. Lahiru Kumara looked good in patches while Akila Dananjaya has been neutralized by the batsmen. However, the experienced campaigner, Suranga Lakmal came good and sent Shai Hope home with a peach. Meanwhile, Devon Smith has been resolute at the crease, even after running out of a few partners. First session of Day 3 has been full of nervy excitement. Second session should be equally entertaining. Catch us in a while.

On a length outside off, Chase tries to guide it away but gets it off the outer half of the bat past the slip cordon. The fielder chases it and slides near the fence to keep the ball in play. Seems like he has done well. Yes, the replays confirm so as he has saved a run for his side. THAT IS LUNCH ON DAY 3!
Good length ball, some extra bounce on that occasion. Chase tries to keep it out but is hit on the thigh pads. No real appeal as that was pretty high.
Similar length ball, angling in, tucked to the leg side.
Shortish delivery, pulled away through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side.

Not Out! Well, there is no surprise at all! Sri Lanka have lost both their reviews. Back of a length ball around leg stump, angling across Smith. He tries to pull it across but is hit on the thigh pad of the back leg. Lakmal puts in a confident appeal but the umpire is unmoved. Chandimal looks interested and after a chat with his teammates, opts for the DRS. Doesn't look a sensible call at all. The Hawk Eye rolls in. Well, the ball is pitching outside the leg stump and that is the end of the story.
Sri Lanka review an LBW decision against Devon Smith. It looks really high to the naked eye. However, are we in for a surprise?
Another one that goes past the defense of Chase to strike him on the pads.
On middle and off, spinning in nicely. Chase leans ahead to block it but misses to get hit on the pads.
Wide down the leg side, the batsman leaves it alone.
Coming in with the arm, tucked with the angle through mid-wicket for a single.
Straighter one from Akila outside off. Smith watches it closely and lets it go.
On a flatter trajectory around off, punched off the back foot towards extra cover.
Short delivery but is down the leg side. Chase ducks under it in a jiffy. A productive over for Lakmal.
Outside off, left alone.
Hangs back to the length ball and defends it nicely.
Roston Chase walks out to bat.

OUT! Lakmal delivers straightaway! Much-needed wicket for the visitors and they are ecstatic. He steams in and bowls a shortish ball on off. The line is such that Shai Hope has to play at it. He does play at it but is in an uncomfortable position. An outside edge is induced. Dhananjaya de Silva at first slip is cool as a cucumber and pouches it safely. The hosts are still 104 runs behind.
In the zone outside off, left alone.
Back of a length ball around off, Hope hops and blocks it right under his eyes.
Suranga Lakmal comes into the attack. Meanwhile, umpire Ian Gould inspects the condition of the ball to ensure that it is not being misused.
On middle and leg, clipped nicely through mid-wicket for a brace.
Sits deep in the crease to this one and keeps it out watchfully.
Loopy delivery from Akila as the batsman milks it down to long on for a single.
Nervy! Shorter in length, spinning in. Hope is not decisive with his footwork but somehow defends it on the track.
This time he is able to get it past the same side of the bowler through mid on. A run taken.
Tossed up ball, drifting in. Smith is on the move as he pushes it towards the left side of the bowler.
Oh my goodness! That kept alarmingly low. Good length ball outside off, doesn't bounce at all as Hope tries to defend it off the back foot but gets foxed.
Length ball outside off, seaming in after landing. Shai shuffles back and across to block it nicely.
Good length ball outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Exquisite! Kumara tries to surprise Hope with a yorker but ends up overpitching it outside off. It is in the zone for the right-hander. He leans ahead and caresses it through covers to find the fence.
Straying on the hips, Hope tucks it nicely through backward square leg. Some work for the fine leg fielder to his left and he does well to keep it down to a couple.
Shaping in sharply on a good length, defended nicely with a straight bat.
In line of the stumps, played with soft hands towards mid on.
On a fuller length, some extra bounce there. Hope tucks it past leg gully for a single.
FOUR! A valiant effort goes in vain. Tossed up ball on a full length outside off, Hope slices it through point. Kumara hares after it, slides near the fence but fails to keep the ball in play.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full delivery, knocked down through mid on to rotate strike.
Shorter in length, kept out nicely.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, Hope does well to block it down the pitch. An aggressive over from Kumara comes to an end.
A pretty well-directed bouncer directed towards the body. Hope sits under it in a flash.
Back of a length ball, defended from within the crease.

That was a lethal, lethal delivery! Could have well gone through the defense. Pinpoint yorker, a toe crusher at 143 kph. Hope is alert to it and just about jams it out but loses his balance after that. Kumara appeals for an LBW but the umpire stays put. The replays show that it clearly came off the bat.
Shortish ball outside off, shaping in. Shai Hope hops and keeps it down towards gully.
Leg bye! Fuller in length around middle and leg, Smith tries to clip it across but the ball brushes his pads and rolls towards square leg. A run taken.
Quicker one outside off, driven crisply towards wide mid off for a brisk single.
Fullish in length on middle, clipped away to mid on.
Strides forward to this one and tucks it away to square leg.
Similar line and length from Akila. The southpaw leans ahead and defends it tentatively towards the vacant short leg region.
Drifting down the leg side, Smith tries to help it away but misses.
On middle and leg, played defensively towards the leg side.
Fuller in length and on the pads, clipped nicely through mid-wicket for a couple.
A leg slip comes into place.
Ooh, that was awkward! Hope misjudged the length there. Short of a length ball, takes off after pitching. Hope is caught in a tangle as he tries to evade it but is hit on the arm.
Good length ball, defended solidly off the back foot.

Good fielding! Length ball around off, Hope comes forward confidently and drives it crisply towards short cover where Perera dives to his right and makes a really good stop. His teammates run towards him and pat him on his back.

This is a good channel. Goes wider of the crease again and lands it in the avenue of apprehension. Good seam presentation from the bowler, it allows him to generate a good amount of inward seam movement. Shai Hope shuffles a touch and makes a good leave.
Kumara bends his back again and bowls this one on a back of a length outside off. Hope arches his back and lets it go.
Straying on the pads this time, played tentatively towards leg gully. Dananjaya starts off his day with a maiden.
Drifting in again, played with soft hands towards mid on.
A leg gully in place now. That is a good field position considering the amount of drift Dananjaya is getting.
Coming in with the arm, tucked with the angle towards short fine leg.
Pitched right up to the batsman as he lunges forward in defense.
A little bit of drift on that one, going down the leg side. Devon tries to help it away but misses.
Tossed up ball on a fullish length on off, Smith leans ahead and defends it nicely.
Akila Dananjaya to roll his arm over now.
Short of a length around off, played with an angled blade towards backward point.

Lahiru Kumara is looking in good shape and is really bending his back. He goes wider of the crease and angles in a back of a length ball. There is some extra bounce on offer. Hope tries to cover the line but the ball flies past the outside edge of his bat.
Shai makes use of the depth of the crease and blocks this one with authority.
On a driveable length outside off, this time Shai Hope strides forward confidently and defends it right under his eyes.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, Hope leans into it and eases it through cover-point. The fielder from the point region runs after it and keeps it down to a couple.
Length ball, shaping in, tucked with a closed bat face towards mid-wicket.
Shaping in substantially from a back of a length, left alone.
In the corridor of uncertainty, the opener shuffles a touch and blocks it with a straight bat.
Two Byes! Similar length ball outside off, stays a bit low. The southpaw lets it go. Dickwella fails to collect it cleanly as the ball rolls behind. A couple of runs are taken.
Good length ball well outside off, Devon doesn't fiddle with it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Straying on the hips, turned towards mid-wicket for a run.
Suranga Lakmal to bowl from the other end.
Short of a length ball on middle and leg, Devon hops and tucks it to the leg side.
No ball! Kumara continues to bowl short but this one is too high. No ball signaled for height.

Umpire Ian Gould is having a discussion with Dickwella. He is not happy with the way Dickwella was appealing. The replays show that once Smith left the crease, the keeper threw the ball on the stumps.

Another short ball, Devon ducks under it in a jiffy. After that, the batsman went out of the crease to do some gardening. Seeing that, Dickwella hits the stumps at the striker's end and appeals but the umpire doesn't go upstairs.
A fierce start from Kumara! Geez, that one took off. Short ball aimed towards the body, Smith shapes for the pull but leaves it at the last moment. The bowler gives him a stare.
Looks like play will start shortly. The umpires have put in the stumps. Yes, we are going to get rolling. Devon Smith is on strike and Lahiru Kumara will bowl to him. Here we go...
The coach, Chandika Hathurusingha has come down to the ground and is seen conveying something to his players. The entire support staff joins in as well. This is getting really frustrating.

The Sri Lankan players are slowly trudging off the field. This is turning into a very serious issue. Their team manager is talking on the phone, perhaps getting some instructions from the Sri Lankan cricket board. The waiting game continues.

Here they come, in a reluctant manner. The fourth umpire is waiting with a box full of balls. It has been finally decided. Lahiru Kumara to steam in with it. Here we go... Chandimal still isn't happy and has an intense conversation with Aleem Dar. Ian Gould joins in as well. The Sri Lankan team manager is discussing something with Javagal Srinath near the dressing room.

Finally, the action is set to get underway. Seems like sanity has prevailed. Devon Smith and Shai Hope walk out to bat. Ian Bishop on air mentions that there is a confirmation that the ball will be changed. The Windies will have a choice regarding which one should be used. A 5-run penalty has also been enforced on Sri Lanka as the umpires feel that they have altered the condition of the ball. However, the away side will be protesting the decision on all fronts. The umpires are still waiting for the visiting team to come out.
Update 1040 Local - We are hearing that play is scheduled to begin in about 10 minutes. Let us hope there are no further delays.
Update 1000 Local - Still no official word as to when the game will begin. Whatever the issue might be, the officials should ensure that the match functions in a smooth manner.
Meanwhile, Ian Gould and Aleem Dar are leaving the field. Seems to be a serious issue. Hopefully, the complication will be sorted out soon.

Bizarre! The entire Sri Lankan team hasn't come out still while the two umpires are waiting in the middle. The Lankan manager is having a serious conversation with the match referee, Javagal Srinath in the dressing room. As we can see on the screen, there is a replay from yesterday which is being shown. Dhananjaya de Silva had the ball with him and was seen shining it. Umpire Ian Gould asked him to show his hands and then had a grim look on his face. Might be a case of the condition of the ball being changed. We are still speculating.

As scheduled, we are on time for the early start. It is good to see a lot of young kids in the stands who are waiting in anticipation for the game to begin. Out come the umpires. Well, there is a little delay. The umpires feel that there is a need to change the ball. Dinesh Chandimal in the dressing room doesn't seem to be happy with it.

PITCH REPORT - Jeff Dujon assessing the track says that there is still a fair amount of green grass on it and there is moisture down there. Adds that the surface is really firm but also mentions that there are a few spots in the good length area from where the ball might take off.

The Windies, on the other hand, are in a pretty comfortable position. Playing some sensible cricket will be their goal. They will be wary that losing a few quick wickets might land them in a tricky situation. You need to fight for every inch in the longest format of the game. Expect an absorbing day of Test cricket.

Hello and a warm welcome to the coverage of Day 3. Clear blue skies greet us at the moment. All eyes will be on the weather as there were continuous interruptions yesterday due to the rain. Be assured that there will be assistance for the pacers on a surface which is already posing uncertainties due to its two-paced nature. However, discipline and consistency is the need of the hour for the visiting bowlers and they need to execute their plans with needle-like precision if they are to threaten the opposition.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

So, we have got news that there will be a half an hour early start tomorrow to make up for the lost overs due to the showers. Another stop-start day is on the cards but let us hope that the rain gods show some mercy. Will the Windies continue to hold the upper hand? Or will the Sri Lankans make an inspirational comeback? Join us on Saturday at 0930 Local (1330 GMT) to catch all the action. Till then, cheers!

Devon Smith is being interviewed on the sidelines. He says that he is familiar with the conditions, knows this pitch better, the bounce and pace. Adds that leaving deliveries outside off and shot selection was good. Further explains that he went after the spinners to take some pressure off his shoulders because the pacers were keeping it tight. Concludes by saying that tomorrow's plan is simple, just bat and bat as long as possible.

Another day which has gone in favour of the home side. They did lose Kieran Powell at the closing stages of play but will be happy with the way they have batted so far. There were intermittent periods of rain after the Lunch break but credit to the hosts for playing sensibly on a surface which had spiced up. They only trail by 135 runs and have a lot of batting to come. The Sri Lankans tried their best with the ball but were not as consistent as they would have liked. Kasun Rajitha and Lahiru Kumara took a wicket apiece. The visitors will need to keep on chipping away at the wickets if they are to come back into the contest.

The umpires have once again got together and have instructed the players to go off the field. Seems like that will be Stumps on Day 2 but we will wait for the official word. Yes, the confirmation has come in. IT IS STUMPS ON DAY 2!
Back of a length outside and the left-hander goes back to his usual self and doesn't go after it.
The umpires, Aleem Dar and Ian Gould are having a conversation. The concern is about the light as two fast bowlers are operating in tandem.

Kumara targets him with the short incoming delivery and Devon slaps it hard from his crease. The ball is hit with power but straight to the fielder at short mid-wicket. Nothing to show for the good shot.
Two gullies in place now.
No, no, no! Lapse in concentration perhaps? Smith has been consistent with not going after the short and wide deliveries but couldn't hold back this time. Lucky for him, the ball misses his edge.
Gets one in his half and drives it through covers off the front foot for two.
OOH! Much more closer to Hope but still no edge. The new batsman has survived, barely.
In the same corridor of uncertainty outside off and the batsman holds his bat close to his body and doesn't flirt with danger. The ball thuds into the keeper's gloves.
Leg Bye! Hits the deck and angles it into the batsman but it is too straight. Hits him on his thigh pad and one run stolen from the leg side.
On a shortish length outside off and Smith lets it pass.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Back of a length around off and Hope chooses to leave it.
On a similar short of a length and jags back in sharply. Hope keeps his willow away from the line and lets it be.
Short of a length and left alone by the batsman.
A play and a miss. Similar length around off and Shai plays for the line but misses as the ball goes past the outside edge.
Back of a length angled into the batsman, takes extra bounce off the pitch and hits high on Hope's bat.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Well outside off and left alone.
On a good length once again and Smith gets forward to defend it but gets hits on the splice.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
On a length outside off, pushed off the back foot by Smith.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Smith lets the ball go outside his off stump. Touch close to the off stump but a good leave in the end.
Shai Hope strides out to bat.

OUT! Gone! Kumara has his man. He has been a bit wayward at times but has managed to bowl a peach when required. Changes the angle once again, goes 'round the wicket. He lands it on a fullish length and gets it to seam away from the pitch. Powell pushes at the ball tentatively with his front foot still in the air and weight not going into the shot. He gets a thick outside edge and Kusal Mendis from second slip dives across to his right in front of first slip and takes a very good catch. Excellent stuff from the bowler and equally well-supported by the fielding department. Windies lose their second wicket and the dangerous looking 56-run partnership has been broken. The hosts trail by 138 runs.
Back of a length, on his hips, tucked away straight to the short square leg fielder.
Tries to bowl a yorker but dishes out a low full toss. The batsman gets it to the leg side from the inside half.
Wide! Unusual bounce. Too high to worry the batsman! Wide signalled by the umpire.
Changes his angle and goes over the wicket to use the short ball better. Digs one in into the body of Powell who does well to sway away from the line and leave it for the keeper.
Touch short this time and fended from his crease with a straight bat.
Around the wicket, angling into the stumps from the good length and blocked by the batsman.
Nice positive stride from Smith. A fuller one around off and driven off the front foot through covers for a couple.
Comes again with the angle from back of a length. The batsman gets his bat up and plays it down from his crease.
Too wide to entice the batsman with a shot.
Effort ball into the ribs of Kieran who tucks it to the vacant mid-wicket region. One run added to the total.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through outside his off stump.
Wide! Too wide and out of the reach of the batsman. Wide signalled by the umpire.
Back of a length and that slinging action takes it to the leg stump, the batsman flicks it to square leg and changes strike.
Kasun Rajitha to bowl from the other end.

And this one passes close to the outside edge. Excitement straightaway after the extended Tea break. Back of a length and angling into Powell, the ball lands on the seam and moves away a touch to square the batsman up. He tries to defend it but is beaten all ends up.

FOUR! Bang! Right out of the screws from Powell. He gets a full delivery around off and creams it off the front foot through extra cover. Positive stuff from him and that also brings up the 50-run stand between the two.
OOH! Arches his back and extracts some extra bounce from short of a length. Powell does well to ride it and keep it down.
Pulls his length back and brings it in from the seam and the batsman lets it be outside his off stump.
Starts with a yorker post break. The batsman digs it out to mid on.

The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Play has been extended till 1830 Local time. It will be a tricky period for the hosts. Sri Lanka will be aiming to make optimum use of the helpful conditions. Kieran Powell is the man on strike as Lahiru Kumara begins the proceedings after the break.
Update 1715 Local - The final inspection of the day has worked out well. The official word is that the match is set to resume in 10 minutes. Should be an interesting passage of play.

Update 1655 Local - After the rain eased off, the inspection took place but it hasn't gone according to plan. The umpires feel that the outfield is still not suitable enough to have a final burst of play. They have scheduled another inspection in about 20 minutes provided there is no more interruption. Be with us.
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

The rain has come down thrice in this session forcing the umpires to call for an early TEA ON DAY 2! The Windies continue to hold the upper hand at this stage. Only 13.1 overs have been possible post Lunch and the hosts haven't lost any more wickets. From the away side's perspective, it has been Lahiru Kumara who has kept the batsmen on their toes but hasn't been able to provide the breakthrough. Devon Smith has gone past a fifty while Kieran Powell is playing the perfect foil for him. The visitors need to find a way to put some pressure on the opposition. Let us keep our fingers crossed so that there are no further shower halts in the evening session.

Update 1600 Local - Another stoppage due to rain. When it rains, it pours and that's what is happening in St Lucia since Lunch. It almost feels like someone up there is holding a remote in his hand and pushing the button to open the floodgates, whenever it amuses him.
Another bouncer from Kumara. Powell sits under it in a jiffy.
Slips in a googly. Smith reads it off the pitch and pushes it back to the bowler.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Straighter one from Akila as Smith clips it towards mid-wicket.
Short and room on offer, cut away to covers.
Tentative! Coming in with the arm, Smith leans ahead to defend but only manages to do so with the inner half of the bat.
Wide outside off, left alone.
Beaten convincingly! Back of a length outside off, seams away substantially after pitching. Powell tries to cover the line but he is nowhere close to it.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
The umpires again have a look at the ball. They are passing it through the 8-shaped gauge but it is fine to continue.

Not Out! No, there is no edge! Sri Lanka waste a review. Back of a length ball in that tight off stump channel. It is coming in initially but seams away after landing to go past the hanging bat of Smith. There is an appeal from the Sri Lankans but nothing from the umpire. Chandimal decides to take the DRS anyway. Time for the replays. The Ultra Edge doesn't detect anything.
Sri Lanka feel that they have Kieran Powell caught behind and challenge the decision. The body language of Chandimal is confident. Is there an edge?

7th Test fifty for Devon Smith! It has been a good knock from him so far and he will be eyeing a big one. Shortish ball on middle and leg, he pulls it away to square leg for a single. Raises his bat towards the scanty crowd and gets the applause from them.
Short delivery, Devon ducks under it.
An appeal for an LBW denied! Coming in with the angle from outside off, Powell tries to defend it but gets an inside edge onto his pads.

Close! Some nerves on display. Coming in with the arm and skidding through after pitching. Smith should be forward to that one but opts to hang back. Is late to bring his bat down but the inside edge onto his pads saves him.
Tossed up ball, Kieran drives it with the angle through mid on and takes a run.
On a flatter trajectory this time, defended from within the crease.
Leans ahead confidently to this one and blocks it nicely.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Powell uses his feet to this one and defends it back to the bowler.
There is a fielder at sweeper cover now after the boundary.
That's a jaffa! Unplayable. In the avenue of apprehension, coming in initially but moving the other way after landing. Smith has no chance but to play at it and is beaten all ends up.
FOUR! Cracking shot! Fractionally overpitched outside off, Smith frees his arms and drills it through covers to find the fence. He moves to 49 with that and the Windies also go past 100 runs.
Length ball outside off, played with soft hands towards covers for an easy single.
The batsman drives the ball straight down the ground.

Russell Arnold makes a comparison between the way Smith and Powell play off the front foot. The former struggles as whenever he comes forward, his front foot is in the air, which doesn't allow him to have a solid base. While, the latter is much more assured. He gets to the pitch of the ball, his head is still and he plays with a high elbow. The opener needs to take a leaf out of his partner's book.
Effort ball from Kumara. Powell sits underneath it nicely.
Very full ball on off, shaping in, Powell covers the line and drives it crisply to mid on.
On a fullish length outside off, Devon lets it go.
On a flatter trajectory, Powell makes use of the depth of the crease to knock it down to long on. A single taken.
Gets right forward to the tossed up ball and defends it right under his eyes.
Straighter one from Akila outside off. Kieran has his stumps covered and makes an assured leave.
Spinning away from Powell as he camps back and cuts it towards backward point.
Slow through the air on off, punched off the back foot towards mid on.
Time for spin. Akila Dananjaya to roll his arm over now.

FOUR! Action straightaway after the break! Full length ball around off, asking Smith to go for an ambitious stroke. He does go at it with hard hands and only manages a thick outside edge past the slip cordon.

Good to see some bright sunshine in St Lucia as the players are ready to get underway again after a brief passage of rain. It has been that sort of an unpredictable day. Let us hope that the showers stay away till the close of play. Devon Smith will take strike as Lahiru Kumara runs in to bowl the final ball of the over.

Update 1500 Local - Play has been halted once again. Groundsmen are in the middle and covering the square with covers. Rain is predicted throughout the day. Although the strong winds can take the rain away but time will tell what it's going to be. Stay tuned for further updates.
In the channel outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Nicely controlled! Back of a length ball, angling in, Smith waits for it and plays it with an angled blade. He is able to guide it past the right side of the diving gully fielder and gets the desired result.

Almost, almost! Good stuff from Kumara. He lands it on a driveable length outside off and Smith obliges. However, he goes at it with minimal foot movement. The ball moves away late as well to fox him completely. Kumara has his hands on his head.
Back of a length outside off, an easy leave for the opener.
Shortish delivery around the off stump, Smith shapes for the pull but there is no timing on it whatsoever as the ball goes towards the mid-wicket fielder.
Pitched up again, this time in line of the stumps, Kieran drives it crisply but the ball goes straight to the man at mid off.
There seems to be some issue with the ball as the umpires have a look at it. Well, seems to be fine to get on with it.
Overpitched this time, sliced away through the point region for a couple.
Easy runs on offer. Short and room on offer, Devon Smith punches it past backward point and comes back for three runs.
Outside off, the opener lets it go.

Close shave! This is much, much better from Lakmal. He lands it in the corridor of uncertainty and gets the ball to seam back in. Smith feels he has his off stump covered as he tries to leave it but the judgement is not that great. The ball just goes past the off stump.
Fullish this time but the line is not right. It is on the pads as Powell flicks it away in front of square leg for a single.

Oh no! It has started drizzling again and the groundsmen are slowly making their way in with the covers. No wait! Scratch whatever I have written. The umpires have called back the players. It was just a passing shower as the weather has brightened up again. The play will continue.
Nicely done! Fractionally overpitched just outside off, Smith shuffles across and creams it through covers to come back for a brace. 9 from the over, a good one for the Windies.

Another tight one but safe in the end! Pitched up ball on off, Powell drives it quite hard towards wide mid off and calls his partner through. Chandimal moves swiftly to his right and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. The replays show that Powell's dive ensured he would have made his crease even if that hit.
In the avenue of apprehension this time. The ball pitches and nips away as Kieran covers his off stump and makes a good leave.
Short of a length ball, leaving Powell. He shuffles a touch and plays it with soft hands towards cover-point.

SIX! Wow! That has really traveled, the strong wind has aided the cause. A nothing delivery from Kumara. It is short and wide outside off. Powell rises on his toes and slashes it over the point region. It is going, going and gone all the way.
Tight line from Kumara. It is fullish and attacking the stumps. Powell covers the line and taps it to mid on.
Outside off, this one comes back in. The opener covers his off stump and lets it go again.
This one pitches on a back of a length outside off and seams away. Smith shuffles across and watches it sail through to the keeper.
A bit wider outside off, on a length this time, Smith points his bat skywards to leave it alone.
Lakmal continues to test the opener outside the off stump. It is on a driveable length but Smith resists the temptation.
Short of a length outside off, Devon shuffles across a touch and lets it go.
Change of gloves for Devon Smith.
In the channel outside off, Smith lets it go.

Good shot! Kumara hits the deck hard. This time the ball sits up nicely for Smith. He pulls it all along the ground through mid-wicket. The rain has meant that the outfield has slowed down even more. Rajitha chases it and saves a run for his side.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Camps back to the back of a length ball and tucks it with a closed bat face.
A lot of bounce on that occasion for Kumara. Shortish ball, takes off after landing. Smith shapes for the pull but bails out at the last moment.

If that was a direct hit, it would have been curtains for Powell! Poor judgement from him. Back of a length ball angling across him. He taps it towards cover-point and sets off. Dananjaya attacks the ball and aims for the bull's eye at the bowler's end but misses. Kieran was out of the crease by some margin. He gets a reprieve.

FOUR! Streaky runs! Kumara bowls this one on a fullish length on off, Powell tries to power it down the ground but ends up squirting it off the outer edge. The ball goes past the gully region and races to the fence.
Lahiru Kumara to bowl from the other end.
Short of a length ball well outside off, Devon remains circumspect in approach. A maiden to start with after the break.
Lakmal goes wider of the crease and angles in a length ball. It is not close enough to make the batsman play.
Back of a length ball around off, played with an angled bat towards cover-point.
Another harmless ball, third leave in a row.
Wide outside off, Smith doesn't fiddle with it.
Starts off with a length ball outside off, left alone.

We are all set to begin again. There has been an adjustment in the session timings as we have lost 12 overs. The second session will be from 1430 to 1630 local. There will be a 20-minute Tea break. The final session will go on till 1800 local if the weather permits. Devon Smith and Kieran Powell to resume their innings. Suranga Lakmal to bowl first up after the break.
Update 1410 Local - The inspection has been done by the umpires. They feel that the playing conditions are good enough for the game to resume in about 20 minutes. Stay with us.
Update 1340 Local - There is some good news coming our way. The rain has stopped and the covers are coming off. There will be an inspection in 20 minutes. Be with us for further updates.

Update 1235 Local - It's drizzling! The covers are on and we are in for a delayed start to this session. The rain seems to be getting heavier by the minute. Good thing is that a strong wind is blowing across the stadium and we just hope that it takes away the rain clouds. Stay tuned, we will keep you posted.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

The visiting bowlers bowled their hearts out. Lahiru Kumara was particularly impressive and troubled the batsmen with his pace and nip. However, it was the debutant, Kasun Rajitha who got the much-needed breakthrough at the fag end of the session with a jaffa. There is enough spice on the surface to keep the bowlers interested. Seems that there will be no respite for the batsmen. Join us shortly for the second session.

Session highlights - 25 overs, 63 runs, 1 wicket. The hosts will be happier of the two sides heading into the break. Though they haven't been able to keep the scoreboard ticking fluently, they have been resilient. The opening pair of Brathwaite and Smith struggled to counter the two-paced nature of the track and the disciplined bowling of the Sri Lankans but they did well to play sensibly to stitch a 50-run stand.
Full around off, Smith goes for a cover drive but doesn't get his bat down in time. An inside edge results in a single towards the mid on region and THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 2.
Short around off and blocked off the back foot with the full face of the bat.

The angle with which he is bowling from around the wicket, it is making the deliveries go down the leg side after pitching around off. This one is flicked off the pads to the square leg region and a couple of runs are added to the total.
Back of a length and driven down the ground for nothing.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Touch too straight and on the pads, Powell flicks it and takes a single.
In line of the stumps, kept out watchfully.
Strides forward to this one and taps it to covers.
Fuller in length, coming in with the angle, tucked to the man at mid on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
An appeal for an LBW turned down! Coming in with the arm, Smith tries to block it but seems to have got an inside edge. The replays confirm the same.
Well bowled! Tossed up around off, spinning away sharply. Smith leans ahead to defend but is beaten all ends up.
The umpires are passing the ball through the 8-shaped gauge. Seems to be fine for the moment.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and on to the pads, Powell flicks it to mid-wicket and opens his account. Two runs taken.
Kieran Powell is the new man in.

OUT! Brathwaite wastes a review! Kasun Rajitha, you beauty! This is unplayable. He has been so consistent with his angle, line and length and he gets his reward. Goes wider of the crease once again, bowls it fuller, around off and gets it to straighten from there. Brathwaite has to play at it and all he can manage on that is an edge to the keeper. He got a leading edge off the previous delivery, which was similar to this one. But this time he has no clue and even the best of the best batsman might have not been able to handle it. Rajitha is ecstatic with his first Test wicket and why shouldn't he be! Windies lose one just at the stroke of Lunch.
The Sri Lankans are already celebrating. Brathwaite has been caught behind but he opts for the review.

Almost a wicket here. A nice pacy length delivery around off from Rajitha. The batsman wanted to go across the line but gets squared up. Leading edge is found but it doesn't reach the fielder at wide slip.
Change in field. A man from covers goes to the short mid-wicket position.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Short of a length outside off and played with soft hands to the slip cordon. Good intelligent batting from Brathwaite.
Flighted around off and driven to cover for nothing.
Misjudges the length but adjusts nicely in the end. It's a full delivery around off, Smith goes back in his crease but due to lack of pace, blocks it easily from there.
Loopy delivery around middle. Smith is happy to defend it.
Flatter one outside off and the batsman lets one through.
Touch short, the batsman goes back and blocks it off his pads.
Tossed up around off, Smith plants his foot down and defends it.
Ignores the wider delivery for the keeper.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Leg Bye! Full and targets Smith's pads, who fails to put bat on ball. The ball clips his pads and rolls towards fine leg. A single results.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Works it to the leg side for nothing.
On a good length, angled into the batsman who blocks it nicely from his crease.
Flatter this time, on leg and the batsman fails to make connection.
Loopy delivery around off, Brathwaite comes out of his crease and defends it back to the bowler.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Gets behind the line and blocks it off the front foot.
Tossed up on middle and flicked off the pads for nothing.

FOUR! Dananjaya errs in line this time and the batsman makes full use of it. Flighted outside off, Brathwaite pushes it through the empty cover region for a boundary. The fielder at mid off ran after the ball but failed to stop it.
Another leave outside off to end the eventful over.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

Back of a length, between the stumps, the batsman looks to play it through mid-wicket and closes the face of the bat touch too early. The ball takes the leading edge and goes into the vacant cover region. Single taken in the end.
Gets his bat down in time and pushes it to mid on for nothing.
Similar line and length from Rajitha and Brathwaite plays inside the line and misses.

Straightaway goes 'round the wicket and troubles Smith. Serves it full, around off and enticing the left-hander to go for the cover drive, who does exactly the same thing. His angled blade comes down hard, gets the inside edge and misses the stumps. The ball goes to fine leg and one run is taken.
Kasun Rajitha is back for another spell.
Goes behind and blocks it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flighted full around off and played to mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Touch short and the batsman taps it to point for nothing.
Flighted on off, Smith gets forward and defends it.
Yorker to end the over. Good over from Lahiru. The batsman digs it out nicely.
Shows the full face and blocks it to the bowler.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.

So close! It's a matter of inches you see. First with the DRS and now with the inside edge. Kumara serves it on a good length and brings it in to the batsman. Some extra bounce troubles the right-hander who tries to block it but it goes off the inside edge towards the keeper. That almost kissed the off pole on its way through.
Full and on to his pads, Brathwaite flicks it straight to square leg.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Strays away to leg side but Smith fails to get any contact as the ball thuds into his pads.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat to the loopy off break.
Flat and short and nicely flicked through the legs of the fielder at short leg. The ball goes into the gap between short mid-wicket and square leg and two runs are taken.

SIX! Bang! No half measures from Smith. Goes down the track again and reaches the flighted delivery around off. Hits across the line and the ball sails over the mid-wicket fence. Smith has shifted from first gear to fifth in a couple of deliveries.
FOUR! Another floater and Smith gives charge to it. Gets enough on it to hit it over mid-wicket. First boundary for the left-hander and he can shift gears now.
Starts with a flighted delivery around off. The batsman blocks it off the front foot.
Akila Dananjaya will roll over his arm for the first time this morning.
Blocks the shortish delivery off the back foot.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
FOUR! Yayy! Wide and full, Brathwaite taps it behind point. The ball has enough legs to go to the boundary, finally. To everyone's surprise, this is the first boundary of the Windies innings.
Leg Bye! Ball hits the batsman low on the pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Short and into the body, Smith goes for the pull but fails to get good connection. The ball gets behind the diving keeper and two runs are added to the total.

Kumara is doing something different here. He is making both the batsmen play and is not wasting energy by bowling wider deliveries. This one lands on a good length and goes away from the left-hander after pitching, who does well to block it.
Jags back in with the angle from back of a length, the batsman clips it off his hips and takes a single from the square leg region.
Similar length outside off, punched to point for nothing.
Short of a length and into the rib cage, Smith dabs it straight to the square leg fielder.
Changes the angle again but serves it touch too wide. The batsman ignores it.
Full and outside, left alone by Smith.
Too straight on the pads and flicked to the square leg region for a single.
Time for Drinks.
Gets fuller and on the stumps, Brathwaite drives it to the vacant wide long on region. Three runs taken.
Short of a length and defended off the back foot by the batsman.

OH! Where did this come from? This pitch is playing a cruel game with the batsman as well as with the bowler. The ball lands on a fullish length, around off and seams away after pitching. Brathwaite hangs his bat but fails to make any connection.
Angled in and down the leg side again. This time, the eeper collects it cleanly.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Four Byes! Free runs for the Windies. Too straight and down the leg side and seams even more after pitching. The keeper dives to his left to stop it but fails. Welcome boundary for the hosts.
There is a bit of drizzle in the air. Let us hope it is a passing shower. The groundsmen are getting ready with the covers.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Back of a length, on middle and leg, flicked to square leg for a single.
As soon as the ball is near the off stump area, on a short of a length, it has done something off the pitch. This one is no different but all it's missing is the edge of the batsman.
Full around off and driven uppishly to point for nothing.
Corrects his line but goes down the leg side. Brathwaite lets it be.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
A play and a miss to end the over. Smith is still in the middle but he isn't giving any confidence to his team.
Smith shoulders arms to let that one through.
Back of a length into the stumps and the batsman gets inside the line and flicks it off his pads. One run added to the total.
Around middle and leg and driven through to mid on for nothing.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Safe! Sri Lanka do not lose a review though. Skiddy action of Kumara gets the ball to jag back in from a length and hits Brathwaite on the flap of his pad. A huge LBW appeal follows from the bowler and the fielding team. Looks so very close but Aleem Dar is unmoved. Kumara seems confident and Chandimal takes the review. The Snickometer suggests that no bat is involved. Time for the Hawk Eye. The ball hits him a bit too high and it's umpire's call in the end. Brathwaite survives a scare.
An LBW review against Kraigg Brathwaite has been taken upstairs. Height seems to be an issue.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Nicely done. A full delivery on the pads and played down the ground with a straight bat. The ball rolls and stops just inside the boundary line and three runs are taken. Not a bad shot eh?
That angle from Kasun is troubling Smith a lot. Darts the fuller delivery in but touch down the leg side as the ball thuds into his pads.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground for nothing.
Shaping in, on a similar length and the batsman flicks it through mid-wicket and runs two. Some venom on these deliveries from Rajitha.

OOH! Almost had him. This one comes in sharply and almost does the trick. Rajitha is maintaining the same angle to the left-hander, on a fuller length, outside off and coming in. Smith is beaten all ends up but the ball takes the inside edge of his bat before hitting his pads and that is what saves him as well. The huge LBW appeal fell on deaf ears.
Can i say it was a repeat telecast of the previous delivery because it was. Great couple of deliveries to end the over.
140 kph delivery from Lahiru and it is on a beautiful channel to the right-hander. Dishes it around off on a good length and makes the batsman play at it, who complies but fails to make connection.
Some chin music for the batsman, he lets that bouncer through to the wicket-keeper.
Similar length and line and this one goes the other way. The batsman shoulder his arms.

Bit of extra pace, hitting the deck hard and getting purchase off the pitch. The ball lands on a short of a length, lands around off and seams away after pitching. The batsman looks to get behind it but misses.
Back of a length, around off, defended from the crease to the off side. One run taken.
Lahiru Kumara is into the attack.
This is much better from the youngster. He runs in hard and generates some late away shape on the ball. Brathwaite shapes for the drive but sensibly lets it go.
